principles: Move code verbatim; a migration that rewrites is no longer a migration and loses the source repo proven behavior.
Put the seam where the source already put it: createApp and startServer are the documented library surface, so packages/main holds only a thin handler.
Build output never enters source control; it is regenerated by the build from declared dependencies.
Never dirty the repository being inspected, because DONE is gated on a clean tree.
Prefer the existing precedent over a new mechanism: dashboard already establishes how a long-running server command dispatches.
drivers: The user asked for a migration into a command, not a redesign.
The web shell plus vendored bundles are large (9325 source lines, roughly 4.6MB of vendor bundles) and must not weigh down packages/main, which every command loads.
node:sqlite forces a Node floor this repository has never declared anywhere.
packages/main cannot ship static assets today, so asset hosting decides the package boundary.
The recursive tsc gate and the eight fail-closed command surfaces punish a partial registration immediately.

options.name: A: new packages/graph subpackage
pros: Keeps the 9325-line web shell and the vendored asset tree out of packages/main.
Places every migrated line under the repository recursive tsc gate.
Matches the boundary the source README already designates (createApp / startServer as the CLI seam).
Asset hosting works naturally because the package that owns the assets also serves them.
The Node engines floor is scoped to the one subpackage that actually needs it.
cons: Adds a fourth package to a repo with no npm workspaces, so the root build chain needs a new explicit entry.
packages/main must resolve the packages/graph package root at runtime to find assets.

options.name: B: merge into packages/main
pros: No new package and no cross-package resolution: everything is inside packages/main.
Single build step, nothing to chain.
cons: Mixes a large browser shell with CLI logic in the package every command loads.
packages/main ships no static assets today and has no files field, so the browser client would need a new asset-copy step in the build plus a change to the build-binding hash.
Forces the node:sqlite Node floor onto the entire CLI rather than one optional subcommand.

options.name: C: consume as npm dependency
pros: Zero code movement; the source package stays authoritative.
packages/main only needs a dependency and a thin call.
cons: The code stays outside this repository validate and recursive tsc gates.
Requires publishing to npm or a file: link, and the story explicitly excludes registry publication.
The user asked for the functionality to live in this repo, which this does not deliver.

rationale: Option A is the only one that satisfies both hard constraints simultaneously. packages/main ships zero static web assets and has no files field, so hosting the browser client there (option B) would require inventing an asset pipeline and amending the build-binding hash, and would additionally impose the node:sqlite Node 22.5 floor on every CLI invocation rather than on one optional subcommand. Option C leaves the code outside the repository gates and needs the npm publication the user excluded. Option A also matches the seam the source package already documents and was built for, so the migration is a copy plus a thin handler rather than a redesign. The cost is one new entry in the root build chain, which is cheap and explicit given this repo has no npm workspaces.

preMortem.scenario: The graph handler cannot locate packages/graph assets once packages/main is installed globally rather than run from the repo, so the served page 404s on app.html.
preMortem.trigger: proof-or-stop graph serves a page that reports app.html missing, or every vendor route returns not installed.
preMortem.consequence: The command appears registered and starts a server, but the graph never renders, which is worse than failing loudly.
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve the packages/graph root via createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve of the package entry rather than a relative __dirname walk, and fail with an explicit message naming the missing asset directory and the build command that produces it.

preMortem.scenario: The new packages/graph tsconfig is picked up by the recursive tsc gate before its dependencies are installed, so validate --lint and pre-push fail for everyone.
preMortem.trigger: npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/graph errors with cannot find module d3 or node:sqlite type errors.
preMortem.consequence: A green repo turns red for every unrelated story, and the pre-push hook blocks pushes.
preMortem.mitigation: Verify npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/graph passes from a clean checkout state before REVIEW, and confirm the recursive gate result on the whole repo rather than only the new package.

preMortem.scenario: Adding the command to only some of the eight registration surfaces leaves a contract test failing, or worse, a command that help lists but dispatch cannot find.
preMortem.trigger: command-ownership-contract or orphan-surface fails, or proof-or-stop graph reports handler not found.
preMortem.consequence: REVIEW to TEST is blocked by the CLI preflight gate, and the command is half-registered in a way that is confusing to diagnose.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat the eight surfaces as one atomic checklist item (CHK-003) and run command-ownership-contract, command-catalog-smoke, cli-surface-smoke and verify-orphan-surface as its acceptance evidence rather than after the fact.

preMortem.scenario: Running the command inside a story worktree writes something into the tree, breaking the clean-tree DONE gate for whichever story is being inspected.
preMortem.trigger: git status is non-empty after running proof-or-stop graph.
preMortem.consequence: The tool silently sabotages the lifecycle gate it exists to visualize.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert git status is byte-identical before and after as CHK-005 acceptance evidence, and confirm no discovery file is written into the project the way .lattice-serve.json is.

preMortem.scenario: The vendored bundles get committed because the copied .gitignore is not carried over or is overridden by a parent ignore rule.
preMortem.trigger: git status shows packages/graph/assets/mermaid.min.js and friends as untracked or staged additions.
preMortem.consequence: Roughly 4.6MB of regenerable binaries enter history, against an explicit user constraint.
preMortem.mitigation: Copy the source .gitignore into packages/graph and verify git check-ignore reports the assets paths as ignored before any commit.
